mutation_targets.rationale: This fact enforces that permitted accesses must have an active care-team membership. Removing it allows the model to construct permitted accesses without the required membership, which is the exact violation OwnershipBasedAccess is designed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some ae: AuditEntry, u: User, p: Patient | ae.clinician = u and ae.patient_id = p.id and ae.outcome = Permitted and no ctm: CareTeamMembership | ctm.clinician = u and ctm.patient = p and ctm.status = Active }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact prevents two distinct audit entries from having the same (clinician, patient_id, occurred_at) key but different outcomes. Removing it allows the injection of duplicates with conflicting data, which the AppendOnly assertion should reject.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.clinician = ae2.clinician and ae1.patient_id = ae2.patient_id and ae1.occurred_at = ae2.occurred_at and ae1.outcome != ae2.outcome }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact ensures audit-entry snapshots (clinician_display_name, clinician_role) match the actual user data. Removing it allows mismatches, which the AttributionCorrectness assertion should catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.clinician_display_name != ae.clinician.display_name or ae.clinician_role != ae.clinician.role }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact enforces the internal distinction: Denied outcomes require an existing patient (clinician not on care team), and NotFoundOrDenied requires patient absence. Removing it allows violations where the outcome doesn't match patient existence, which NoInformationLeakage detects.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InformationLeakageViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | (ae.outcome = Denied and no p: Patient | p.id = ae.patient_id) or (ae.outcome = NotFoundOrDenied and some p: Patient | p.id = ae.patient_id) }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact enforces that only clinical roles (not AuditOfficer) appear in the audit log for patient-record accesses. Removing it allows AuditOfficer entries, which violates the role-separation invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_RoleSeparationViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.clinician.role = AuditOfficer }
